p0000: MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

p0001: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Redwood Commerce Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Silverline Systems Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.

p0002: 1. DEFINITIONS

p0003: 1.1 “Affiliate” means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party. “Control” means ownership of more than fifty percent of the voting interests of an entity or the power to direct its management. An entity is an Affiliate only while that relationship continues.

p0004: 1.2 “Applicable Law” means every statute, regulation, binding regulatory requirement, court order, and governmental rule applicable to a Party's performance under this Agreement, including laws concerning privacy, information security, export controls, employment, anti-bribery, and accessibility. Applicable Law does not include a private standard unless an Order Form expressly adopts it.

p0005: 1.3 “Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.

p0006: 1.4 “Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.

p0007: 1.5 “Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.

p0008: 1.6 “Order Form” means a written ordering document signed by authorized representatives of both Parties that references this Agreement and describes the Services, Deliverables, subscription quantities, service levels, Fees, and term purchased by Customer. A purchase order is an administrative convenience only and does not amend an Order Form or this Agreement.

p0009: 1.7 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

p0010: 1.8 “Vendor Technology” means Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, documentation, routines, connectors, and other technology, and modifications of them that are not Deliverables and do not embody Customer Confidential Information. Vendor Technology does not include Customer Data or intellectual property owned by Customer before the Effective Date.

p0011: 2. AGREEMENT STRUCTURE AND SCOPE

p0012: 2.1 This Agreement establishes the legal terms under which Customer and its Affiliates may purchase Services from Vendor. No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.

p0013: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.

p0014: 2.2 Each Order Form is governed by this Agreement. If provisions conflict, the following order controls: a signed amendment that expressly identifies the provision amended; the applicable Order Form; any service-level exhibit; any security exhibit; and this Agreement. An Order Form prevails only for that Order Form and only when it expressly identifies the conflicting provision.

p0015: 2.3 Vendor terms appearing on a website, click-through screen, invoice, quotation, acknowledgement, support portal, or purchase-order response do not apply, even if access to the Services technically requires acceptance. Customer's use of or payment for Services does not assent to additional or different terms.

p0016: 3. SERVICES AND PERFORMANCE

p0017: 3.1 Vendor shall provide the Services professionally, diligently, and in accordance with this Agreement, each Order Form, the documentation, agreed project plans, and Applicable Law. Vendor is responsible for the acts and omissions of its personnel, Affiliates, and subcontractors as though they were Vendor's own.

p0018: 4. ORDER FORMS AND AFFILIATE ORDERS

p0019: 4.1 An Order Form becomes binding when signed by both Parties. Changes in scope, assumptions, quantities, Fees, dependencies, or dates require a written change order signed by authorized representatives. Vendor shall not charge for work outside scope that Customer did not approve in a signed change order.

p0020: 5. IMPLEMENTATION AND CHANGE CONTROL

p0021: 5.1 Vendor shall prepare and maintain an implementation plan identifying tasks, owners, assumptions, dependencies, deliverables, acceptance criteria, risks, and target dates. The Parties will hold regular status meetings during implementation. Vendor shall keep accurate action and decision logs and furnish them to Customer on request.

p0022: 6. ACCEPTANCE

p0023: 6.1 Customer will have fifteen business days after delivery of a Deliverable to test it against the acceptance criteria in the applicable Order Form. Customer may accept it in writing or reject it by describing material nonconformities. Payment, productive use needed for testing, or silence does not constitute acceptance.

p0024: 6.2 If Customer rejects a Deliverable, Vendor shall promptly correct the nonconformities at no additional charge and resubmit it for a new acceptance period. After two unsuccessful correction cycles, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and receive a refund of Fees paid for the rejected Deliverable and dependent Services Customer cannot reasonably use.

p0025: 7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

p0026: 7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

p0027: 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.

p0028: 7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

p0029: 7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

p0030: 7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

p0031: 7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.

p0032: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.

p0033: 8. TERM AND RENEWAL

p0034: 8.1 This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.

p0035: 8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.

p0036: 8.3 On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.

p0037: 9. TERMINATION

p0038: 9.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.

p0039: 9.2 Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.

p0040: 9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.

p0041: 9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.

p0042: 10. EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION

p0043: 10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.

p0044: 10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.

p0045: 11. TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND DATA RETURN

p0046: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.

p0047: 11.2 Within thirty days after Customer's request, Vendor shall return all Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with relationships and metadata reasonably necessary for use. Vendor shall not withhold Customer Data because of a fee dispute.

p0048: 11.3 After Customer confirms successful return, Vendor shall securely delete remaining Customer Data from active systems and, as backups cycle, from backups, except for a copy required by Applicable Law. An authorized officer shall certify deletion in writing. Any retained copy remains protected and may not be used for another purpose.

p0049: 12. CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES

p0050: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.

p0051: 12.4 For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.

p0052: 13. ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE

p0053: 13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.

p0054: 13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.

p0055: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.

p0056: 13.4 Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.

p0057: 14. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES

p0058: 14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.

p0059: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.

p0060: 14.3 Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.

p0061: 14.4 No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.

p0062: 15. CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY

p0063: 15.1 Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, to provide the Services, and as permitted by this Agreement. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data, use it for advertising, combine it with another customer's identifiable data, or train a generally available model on it without Customer's express written consent.

p0064: 15.2 Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law concerning personal information. If Vendor processes personal information for Customer, the Parties' data-processing addendum is incorporated. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.

p0065: 16. CONFIDENTIALITY

p0066: 16.1 “Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.

p0067: 16.2 The recipient shall use Confidential Information only to perform or exercise rights under this Agreement, protect it with at least reasonable care, and disclose it only to personnel, Affiliates, advisers, and subcontractors who need to know and are bound by confidentiality obligations. The recipient is responsible for their unauthorized use or disclosure.

p0068: 16.5 On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.

p0069: 17. INFORMATION SECURITY

p0070: 17.1 Vendor shall maintain a written information-security program using administrative, technical, organizational, and physical safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of Customer Data and risk. At minimum, Vendor shall implement least-privilege access, multifactor authentication, encryption in transit and at rest, secure development, vulnerability management, logging, backup, business continuity, and annual workforce training.

p0071: 17.2 Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay and no later than twenty-four hours after confirming unauthorized access to, acquisition, disclosure, alteration, loss, or destruction of Customer Data or a material compromise of systems used to provide the Services (a “Security Incident”). Notice will include known facts, affected data and systems, containment, and a contact.

p0072: 18. INSURANCE

p0073: 18.1 Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.

p0074: 18.2 Policies will be issued by reputable insurers and be primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary. p0075: 19. WARRANTIES

p0076: 19.1 Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. p0077: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. p0078: 19.3 Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. p0079: 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. p0080: 19.5 Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.

p0081: 20. INDEMNIFICATION

p0082: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.

p0083: 20.2 Vendor shall also defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the Customer indemnified parties from third-party claims to the extent arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; bodily injury, death, or tangible property damage caused by Vendor; unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.

p0084: 20.3 Customer shall defend and indemnify Vendor from a third-party claim alleging that unmodified Customer material supplied by Customer and used by Vendor strictly as authorized infringes an intellectual property right, or arising from Customer's violation of Applicable Law in its authorized use of the Services. p0085: 20.4 The indemnified Party shall give prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, and control of the defence, except delay excuses obligations only to the extent of material prejudice. p0086: 20.5 For an infringement claim, Vendor shall, at its expense and in addition to its defence obligations, procure continued use, modify or replace the affected item without materially reducing functionality, or, if neither is commercially reasonable, terminate the item and refund prepaid and implementation Fees on a straight-line three-year basis. p0087: 21. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

p0088: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.

p0089: 21.2 Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.

p0090: 21.3 “Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.

p0091: 21.4 The limitations allocate risk between sophisticated Parties and apply only to the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law. Nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.

p0092: 22. AUDIT RIGHTS

p0093: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.

p0094: 22.2 Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.

p0095: 22.3 Audit findings are Customer Confidential Information and may be used only to enforce this Agreement. Vendor shall provide a copy of the final report. Payment of a shortfall resolves the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error.

p0096: 23. RECORDS AND CUSTOMER ASSURANCE

p0097: 24. ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL

p0098: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.

p0099: 24.2 Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.

p0100: 24.3 For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.

p0101: 24.4 Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.

p0102: 25. PUBLICITY AND MARKS

p0103: 25.1 Neither Party may issue a press release naming the other or use the other's names, trademarks, logos, or service marks in publicity, customer lists, case studies, or marketing without prior written consent in each instance. Customer may withdraw consent prospectively.

p0104: 26. COMPLIANCE WITH LAW AND ETHICS

p0105: 26.1 Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law in performing this Agreement. Vendor shall maintain policies reasonably designed to prevent bribery, corruption, forced labour, discrimination, retaliation, and conflicts of interest and shall provide annual compliance training to assigned personnel.

p0106: 26.2 Vendor represents it has not offered and will not offer anything of value to improperly influence an official or private person in connection with this Agreement. Vendor shall maintain accurate books and promptly report a credible suspected violation materially related to the Services.

p0107: 26.3 Each Party shall comply with applicable export-control and sanctions laws. Vendor is responsible for classifying Vendor Technology and identifying restrictions before delivery. Customer will not knowingly permit access from a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction contrary to written notice and Applicable Law.

p0108: 26.4 Vendor shall comply with reasonable Customer workplace, safety, security, and acceptable-use policies supplied in advance while accessing Customer facilities or systems. A policy does not amend commercial terms or impose obligations unrelated to that access.

p0109: 27. FORCE MAJEURE AND BUSINESS CONTINUITY

p0110: 27.1 Neither Party is liable for delay caused by an event beyond its reasonable control that could not have been prevented through reasonable care, excluding inability to pay, staffing shortages, subcontractor failure that could reasonably be avoided, or a cyberattack preventable by required safeguards. The affected Party shall promptly notify the other and mitigate.

p0111: 27.2 Vendor shall maintain and test at least annually business-continuity and disaster-recovery plans appropriate to the Services. Plans will address redundant systems, backups, recovery objectives, communications, and alternate personnel. Vendor shall provide a current executive summary on request.

p0112: 27.3 If a force-majeure event materially prevents an affected Service for more than fifteen consecutive days, Customer may procure substitute services and suspend affected Fees. After thirty consecutive days, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without penalty and receive a refund of prepaid Fees for the unavailable period.

p0113: 28. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

p0114: 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.

p0115: 28.2 The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.

p0116: 28.3 Before filing an ordinary commercial claim, a Party shall give notice and permit executives with settlement authority to meet in good faith within fifteen business days. This process does not delay urgent relief or a filing needed to preserve a limitations period. Discussions are compromise negotiations to the extent allowed by law.

p0117: 29. NOTICES

p0118: 29.1 Legal notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by nationally recognized overnight courier or certified mail, return receipt requested, to the address in the preamble and by email to the legal-notice address stated in the applicable Order Form. Operational notices may be delivered through agreed service channels.

p0119: 29.2 Notice is effective on documented delivery, except a refusal is deemed delivery. A Party may change its notice address by notice under this Section. p0120: 29.3 Notices to Customer must copy legal@northwind.example, and notices to Vendor must copy legal@brightline.example. Automated portal messages, invoices, and website postings are not legal notices.

p0121: 30. GENERAL

p0122: 30.1 The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing creates a partnership, joint venture, fiduciary relationship, franchise, or agency. Neither Party may bind the other. Vendor is solely responsible for compensation, direction, and taxes of its personnel.

p0123: 30.2 Neither Party's failure or delay in exercising a right waives it. A waiver must be written and signed by an authorized representative and applies only to the stated instance. Remedies are cumulative unless an exclusive remedy is expressly identified.

p0124: 30.3 If a court finds a provision unenforceable, it will be modified to the minimum extent needed to make it enforceable while preserving intent, and the remainder continues. Headings aid reference only. “Including” means “including without limitation,” and “or” is inclusive.

p0125: 30.4 This Agreement, its exhibits, and executed Order Forms are the entire agreement about their subject and supersede prior proposals, statements, and agreements. An amendment must be in a writing signed by authorized representatives of both Parties and expressly identify this Agreement.

p0126: 30.5 No person other than a Party, a Customer Affiliate ordering Services, a permitted successor, or an indemnified party has a right to enforce this Agreement. The Parties may amend or terminate it without another person's consent, subject to vested indemnity rights.

p0127: 30.6 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, each treated as an original, and by electronic signature. An electronic copy is effective as an original. Each signatory represents that they are authorized to bind the named Party.

p0128: 30.7 Vendor shall not use an artificial-intelligence system to make a legally binding decision for Customer or submit Customer Confidential Information to a third-party model unless an Order Form expressly authorizes that use and specifies safeguards. Vendor remains responsible for output used in providing the Services.

# MSA Review — Redwood Commerce Group (Customer) / Silverline Systems Ltd. (Vendor)

**Overall:** The body of this MSA is unusually customer-favorable (IP assignment, perpetual embedded-tech licence, 45-day terms, mutual cap with broad Excluded Claims, data return, transition assistance). However, **six clauses are materially off-market against Customer and contradict the rest of the document** — they read as inserted terms and should be struck or rewritten. There are also several **structural gaps** (no SLA, no security assurance rights, empty Section 23, duplicate numbering) and a **conflict-of-terms hierarchy that subordinates the negotiated MSA to vendor exhibits**.

Positions below are market-standard customer positions; I have not applied a company playbook.

---

## A. Priority 1 — Strike or rewrite (material, one-sided, internally inconsistent)

**1. Exclusivity — p0013 (first "2.2")**
"Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term." This locks Customer out of all other analytics providers for three years with no volume commitment, pricing protection, or performance condition, and it **directly contradicts p0012 (2.1) and p0050 (12.3)**.
→ **Delete in full.** If Vendor insists, cap at a named product line, condition on continuous SLA compliance and competitive pricing, and add a Customer right to terminate exclusivity on notice.

**2. Most-favoured-supplier obligation — p0027 (first "7.2")**
"Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier." This is an MFN *against* Customer, unbounded, unauditable, and inconsistent with p0050 (12.3), which recites that no MFC commitment exists. It also implicitly requires disclosure of other suppliers' confidential terms.
→ **Delete in full.** No substitute.

**3. Liquidated damages against Customer — p0032 (7.6)**
USD 25,000/day for "any delay in providing a dependency." No definition of "dependency" (note Section 12 is missing 12.1–12.2, so Customer responsibilities are undefined), no materiality threshold, no notice/cure, no cap, and no showing of actual loss — likely an unenforceable penalty under NY law, but litigation-inviting and one-sided (Vendor bears no reciprocal LDs for missed dates).
→ **Delete.** Replace with the standard excusable-delay construct:

> *"If Customer fails to perform a dependency expressly identified in the applicable Order Form or implementation plan, and that failure actually and materially delays Vendor's performance, Vendor's affected dates will be extended day-for-day and Vendor may recover documented, reasonable idle-resource costs actually incurred, provided Vendor gave Customer written notice of the dependency failure and a reasonable opportunity (not less than ten business days) to cure. This is Vendor's sole remedy for Customer delay."*

**4. Auto-renewal with 180-day notice — p0035 (8.2)**
Evergreen 12-month renewals requiring notice six months before each anniversary; a missed diary entry commits Customer to a further year at CPI/3% uplift (p0036).
→ **Reduce non-renewal notice to 30–60 days** and, preferably, make renewal at Customer's election:

> *"Each Order Form expires at the end of its stated term unless Customer elects renewal in writing. If an Order Form provides for automatic renewal, either Party may prevent renewal by written notice at least thirty (30) days before the end of the then-current term."*

**5. Non-solicit / no-hire — p0051 (12.4)**
"Any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term," for 18 months, covering *engagement* as well as solicitation. This is effectively a no-hire covering Vendor's entire workforce (including people Customer never met), is unilateral, and contradicts p0050 (12.3), which expressly preserves Customer's right to hire responders to general recruitment.
→ **Rewrite as mutual and narrow:**

> *"During the term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, neither Party will knowingly solicit for employment any employee of the other who was directly and substantially engaged in performing or receiving the Services. This does not restrict general advertising, recruiter searches not targeted at the other Party, or hiring any person who responds to such efforts or who approaches a Party unsolicited."*

**6. Vendor audit of Customer — p0093 (22.1)**
"Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records." Unlimited, unannounced, and remote-access rights are unacceptable (privileged material, other suppliers' data, Customer's own security posture) and **contradict p0094 (22.2)**, which bars direct system access.
→ **Replace 22.1 with:**

> *"No more than once per twelve months, on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, Vendor may verify Customer's usage of the Services. Verification will be conducted first by Customer self-certification based on Vendor's own usage telemetry; only if that is reasonably inconclusive may Vendor engage an independent auditor (not a Customer competitor) bound by confidentiality, during business hours, in a manner that does not disrupt Customer's operations. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems, networks, or facilities directly. Vendor bears its own and the auditor's costs, subject to Section 22.2."*

---

## B. Priority 2 — Missing protections (gaps, not bad clauses)

**7. No service levels or service credits.** Section 3 contains only 3.1. Yet p0007 (1.5) references "service credits," p0014 (2.2) references a "service-level exhibit," and p0040 (9.3) gives termination for repeatedly missing a "critical service level" — none of which exist in this document. As drafted, Customer has **no remedy for downtime** short of material-breach termination.
→ Attach an SLA exhibit before signature: uptime commitment (e.g., 99.9% excluding properly noticed maintenance), support response/resolution targets, automatic credits without a claim requirement, chronic-failure termination right with refund, and an express statement that **credits are not Customer's sole or exclusive remedy** and do not limit Section 21.

**8. No security assurance or audit rights for Customer; Section 23 is an empty heading (p0096).** Section 17 states substantive controls but gives Customer no way to verify them, and no incident obligations beyond notice.
→ Populate Section 23:

> *"Vendor shall, annually and on request: (a) provide its current SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent) report and remediation plan for any exceptions; (b) provide an executive summary of its most recent independent penetration test and confirmation of remediation of high/critical findings; (c) complete Customer's reasonable security questionnaire; and (d) on a Security Incident or material control failure, permit Customer or its independent assessor to audit Vendor's controls relevant to Customer Data. Vendor shall retain records sufficient to verify Fees, usage, and compliance for three years and make them available on reasonable notice."*

Also add to 17.2: Vendor must investigate, contain, and remediate at its cost; preserve forensic evidence; cooperate with Customer's investigation; **not notify regulators, data subjects, or the public in a manner identifying Customer without Customer's prior written consent** (except as legally required); and bear reasonable notification, credit-monitoring, and call-centre costs where the incident arises from Vendor's failure.

**9. No subcontractor / subprocessor controls.** p0017 (3.1) makes Vendor responsible for subcontractors, but there is no approval, notice, objection, or flow-down right, and no data-location commitment.
→ Add: prior written notice of new material subcontractors/subprocessors handling Customer Data, a Customer objection right (with termination of affected Services if unresolved), mandatory flow-down of Sections 15–17, and a data-residency commitment (specify permitted regions) with no cross-border transfer without Customer consent and a valid transfer mechanism.

**10. Missing exhibits are referenced as incorporated.** p0064 (15.2) incorporates "the Parties' data-processing addendum"; p0014 and p0056 reference security and service-level exhibits. None are attached.
→ Do not sign until the DPA, security exhibit, and SLA are attached and cross-referenced by title and date. Confirm the DPA covers CCPA/CPRA service-provider language, GDPR/UK Art. 28 terms, SCCs if applicable, sub-processor terms, and deletion/return consistent with Section 11.

**11. No Customer termination for convenience.** Customer can exit only for breach, insolvency, security/SLA/legal failures (9.1–9.3) or force majeure (27.3).
→ Add: *"Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience on sixty (60) days' written notice; Vendor will refund prepaid Fees for the terminated period and Customer will pay for Services performed and non-cancellable third-party costs actually incurred through the effective date."* At minimum secure this for professional-services Order Forms.

**12. No survival clause.** There is no provision listing surviving sections (confidentiality, IP, indemnity, liability, data return, transition, governing law).
→ Add a standard survival provision to Section 30.

---

## C. Priority 3 — Drafting and consistency issues

| Cite | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| p0014 (2.2) | Order of precedence puts **this Agreement last**, below Order Forms and Vendor's SLA/security exhibits — vendor forms can dilute negotiated MSA terms (partially mitigated by the "expressly identifies" requirement). | Carve out core terms: *"Notwithstanding the foregoing, Sections 13–17, 19–21, and 24 of this Agreement control over any Order Form or exhibit unless a signed amendment expressly amends the specific provision."* |
| p0013/p0014; p0027/p0028 | **Two clauses numbered 2.2 and two numbered 7.2.** Also missing 9.4, 12.1–12.2, 16.3–16.4, and Section 23 text. | Renumber; confirm no omitted text was intended (particularly Customer Responsibilities 12.1–12.2, which the deleted LD clause depended on). |
| p0120 (29.3) | Notice copy addresses are **@northwind.example** and **@brightline.example** — neither Party is Northwind or Brightline. Suggests text lifted from another agreement. | Replace with correct Redwood and Silverline legal-notice addresses; conform to the entity names in p0001. |
| p0001 | Vendor named "Silverline Systems **Ltd.**, a New York **corporation**." | Verify exact legal entity, jurisdiction, and good standing; confirm the contracting entity is the one that owns the IP and operates the hosting environment. |
| p0058 (14.1) vs p0063 (15.1) | 14.1 licenses Vendor to process Customer Data to "**improve** the Services"; 15.1 prohibits model training and cross-customer combination. Ambiguity Vendor could exploit. | Amend 14.1 to *"solely to provide, secure, and support the Services for Customer"* and delete "improve," or subject "improve" expressly to Section 15.1. |
| p0005 (1.3) | Customer Data excludes "anonymized operational telemetry." | Add: *"Vendor may use such telemetry only in aggregated, de-identified form for service operation and improvement, will not attempt re-identification, and will not disclose it in a manner identifying Customer."* |
| p0078 (19.3) | Malicious-code warranty limited to code "**intentionally introduced by Vendor**" — excludes negligently transmitted malware. | Change to: *"the Services and Deliverables will be free of viruses, malware, and other malicious code, and Vendor will use current-generation scanning tools to detect and prevent the same."* Remove "intentionally introduced by Vendor." |
| p0073 (18.1) | Cyber limit of USD 5M and E&O of USD 2M sit against **uncapped** liability for data/security Excluded Claims; tail is only one year (E&O/cyber are typically claims-made). | Consider cyber at USD 10M and E&O at USD 5M for a hosted analytics platform; extend the tail to **three years** post-termination; require Customer as additional insured on CGL and waiver of subrogation. |
| p0088–p0090 (21.1, 21.3) | Cap is mutual and Excluded Claims are uncapped **both ways** — Customer's exposure under its 20.3 indemnity, confidentiality, and IP is therefore unlimited. | Either cap Customer's indemnity/confidentiality exposure at the general cap (leaving Vendor's data/security exposure uncapped or at a super-cap), or introduce a mutual super-cap (e.g., 3–5× annual Fees) for confidentiality/data claims with Vendor's IP-infringement indemnity remaining uncapped. |
| p0086 (20.5) | Infringement refund is straight-line over three years; may under-compensate on a long-term or heavily implemented deployment. | Amortize over the actual Order Form term, and add refund of implementation Fees in full where Customer cannot reuse the work. |
| p0046 (11.1) | Transition assistance at "the rates in the expiring Order Form" for six months. | Add: extendable by Customer for up to a further six months at the same rates; expressly available **even where termination is for Customer's non-payment**, provided Customer pays transition Fees in advance. |
| p0036 (8.3) | Uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3% — good. | Confirm this applies to **all** recurring Fees across all renewal terms (not just the first) and that unit prices for usage tiers are also fixed or capped. |
| p0028 (7.2) | Annual Fees may be invoiced in advance. | Prefer quarterly or monthly in advance; if annual, tie payment to go-live/acceptance for the initial term. |

---

## D. Suggested handling

1. **Do not sign** until the six Priority 1 clauses are struck/rewritten — items 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 each contradict other clauses in the same document, so Vendor should have little principled basis to resist.
2. **Condition signature** on attachment of the SLA, security exhibit, and DPA (item 10) — the Agreement already assumes they exist.
3. Treat items 7, 8, 9, 11 and 12 as required adds; items in Section C as clean-up in a single consolidated redline.
4. Confirm with the business: whether any exclusivity or MFN was in fact negotiated commercially (p0013/p0027), and whether pricing assumed the deleted liquidated-damages allocation.

*Note: this review is limited to the four corners of the pasted document; I have not reviewed the referenced Order Form(s), SLA, security exhibit, or DPA, and my comments on those are necessarily provisional.*

p0000: MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

p0001: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Redwood Commerce Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Silverline Systems Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.

p0002: 1. DEFINITIONS

p0003: 1.1 “Affiliate” means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party. “Control” means ownership of more than fifty percent of the voting interests of an entity or the power to direct its management. An entity is an Affiliate only while that relationship continues.

p0004: 1.2 “Applicable Law” means every statute, regulation, binding regulatory requirement, court order, and governmental rule applicable to a Party's performance under this Agreement, including laws concerning privacy, information security, export controls, employment, anti-bribery, and accessibility. Applicable Law does not include a private standard unless an Order Form expressly adopts it.

p0005: 1.3 “Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.

p0006: 1.4 “Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.

p0007: 1.5 “Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.

p0008: 1.6 “Order Form” means a written ordering document signed by authorized representatives of both Parties that references this Agreement and describes the Services, Deliverables, subscription quantities, service levels, Fees, and term purchased by Customer. A purchase order is an administrative convenience only and does not amend an Order Form or this Agreement.

p0009: 1.7 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

p0010: 1.8 “Vendor Technology” means Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, documentation, routines, connectors, and other technology, and modifications of them that are not Deliverables and do not embody Customer Confidential Information. Vendor Technology does not include Customer Data or intellectual property owned by Customer before the Effective Date.

p0011: 2. AGREEMENT STRUCTURE AND SCOPE

p0012: 2.1 This Agreement establishes the legal terms under which Customer and its Affiliates may purchase Services from Vendor. No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.

p0013: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.

p0014: 2.2 Each Order Form is governed by this Agreement. If provisions conflict, the following order controls: a signed amendment that expressly identifies the provision amended; the applicable Order Form; any service-level exhibit; any security exhibit; and this Agreement. An Order Form prevails only for that Order Form and only when it expressly identifies the conflicting provision.

p0015: 2.3 Vendor terms appearing on a website, click-through screen, invoice, quotation, acknowledgement, support portal, or purchase-order response do not apply, even if access to the Services technically requires acceptance. Customer's use of or payment for Services does not assent to additional or different terms.

p0016: 3. SERVICES AND PERFORMANCE

p0017: 3.1 Vendor shall provide the Services professionally, diligently, and in accordance with this Agreement, each Order Form, the documentation, agreed project plans, and Applicable Law. Vendor is responsible for the acts and omissions of its personnel, Affiliates, and subcontractors as though they were Vendor's own.

p0018: 4. ORDER FORMS AND AFFILIATE ORDERS

p0019: 4.1 An Order Form becomes binding when signed by both Parties. Changes in scope, assumptions, quantities, Fees, dependencies, or dates require a written change order signed by authorized representatives. Vendor shall not charge for work outside scope that Customer did not approve in a signed change order.

p0020: 5. IMPLEMENTATION AND CHANGE CONTROL

p0021: 5.1 Vendor shall prepare and maintain an implementation plan identifying tasks, owners, assumptions, dependencies, deliverables, acceptance criteria, risks, and target dates. The Parties will hold regular status meetings during implementation. Vendor shall keep accurate action and decision logs and furnish them to Customer on request.

p0022: 6. ACCEPTANCE

p0023: 6.1 Customer will have fifteen business days after delivery of a Deliverable to test it against the acceptance criteria in the applicable Order Form. Customer may accept it in writing or reject it by describing material nonconformities. Payment, productive use needed for testing, or silence does not constitute acceptance.

p0024: 6.2 If Customer rejects a Deliverable, Vendor shall promptly correct the nonconformities at no additional charge and resubmit it for a new acceptance period. After two unsuccessful correction cycles, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and receive a refund of Fees paid for the rejected Deliverable and dependent Services Customer cannot reasonably use.

p0025: 7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

p0026: 7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

p0027: 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.

p0028: 7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

p0029: 7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

p0030: 7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

p0031: 7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.

p0032: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.

p0033: 8. TERM AND RENEWAL

p0034: 8.1 This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.

p0035: 8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.

p0036: 8.3 On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.

p0037: 9. TERMINATION

p0038: 9.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.

p0039: 9.2 Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.

p0040: 9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.

p0041: 9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.

p0042: 10. EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION

p0043: 10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.

p0044: 10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.

p0045: 11. TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND DATA RETURN

p0046: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.

p0047: 11.2 Within thirty days after Customer's request, Vendor shall return all Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with relationships and metadata reasonably necessary for use. Vendor shall not withhold Customer Data because of a fee dispute.

p0048: 11.3 After Customer confirms successful return, Vendor shall securely delete remaining Customer Data from active systems and, as backups cycle, from backups, except for a copy required by Applicable Law. An authorized officer shall certify deletion in writing. Any retained copy remains protected and may not be used for another purpose.

p0049: 12. CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES

p0050: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.

p0051: 12.4 For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.

p0052: 13. ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE

p0053: 13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.

p0054: 13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.

p0055: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.

p0056: 13.4 Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.

p0057: 14. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES

p0058: 14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.

p0059: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.

p0060: 14.3 Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.

p0061: 14.4 No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.

p0062: 15. CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY

p0063: 15.1 Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, to provide the Services, and as permitted by this Agreement. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data, use it for advertising, combine it with another customer's identifiable data, or train a generally available model on it without Customer's express written consent.

p0064: 15.2 Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law concerning personal information. If Vendor processes personal information for Customer, the Parties' data-processing addendum is incorporated. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.

p0065: 16. CONFIDENTIALITY

p0066: 16.1 “Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.

p0067: 16.2 The recipient shall use Confidential Information only to perform or exercise rights under this Agreement, protect it with at least reasonable care, and disclose it only to personnel, Affiliates, advisers, and subcontractors who need to know and are bound by confidentiality obligations. The recipient is responsible for their unauthorized use or disclosure.

p0068: 16.5 On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.

p0069: 17. INFORMATION SECURITY

p0070: 17.1 Vendor shall maintain a written information-security program using administrative, technical, organizational, and physical safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of Customer Data and risk. At minimum, Vendor shall implement least-privilege access, multifactor authentication, encryption in transit and at rest, secure development, vulnerability management, logging, backup, business continuity, and annual workforce training.

p0071: 17.2 Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay and no later than twenty-four hours after confirming unauthorized access to, acquisition, disclosure, alteration, loss, or destruction of Customer Data or a material compromise of systems used to provide the Services (a “Security Incident”). Notice will include known facts, affected data and systems, containment, and a contact.

p0072: 18. INSURANCE

p0073: 18.1 Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.

p0074: 18.2 Policies will be issued by reputable insurers and be primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary. On request, Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance and evidence of relevant coverage. Vendor shall give advance notice of cancellation or material reduction to the extent available from its insurer. Insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.

p0075: 19. WARRANTIES

p0076: 19.1 Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.

p0077: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.

p0078: 19.3 Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.

p0079: 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.

p0080: 19.5 Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.

p0081: 20. INDEMNIFICATION

p0082: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.

p0083: 20.2 Vendor shall also defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the Customer indemnified parties from third-party claims to the extent arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; bodily injury, death, or tangible property damage caused by Vendor; unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.

p0084: 20.3 Customer shall defend and indemnify Vendor from a third-party claim alleging that unmodified Customer material supplied by Customer and used by Vendor strictly as authorized infringes an intellectual property right, or arising from Customer's violation of Applicable Law in its authorized use of the Services. Customer has no obligation to the extent a claim arises from Vendor Technology, modification, combination, or instructions.

p0085: 20.4 The indemnified Party shall give prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, and control of the defence, except delay excuses obligations only to the extent of material prejudice. The indemnifying Party may not settle a claim by admitting fault of, imposing non-monetary obligations on, or failing to fully release the indemnified Party without prior written consent.

p0086: 20.5 For an infringement claim, Vendor shall, at its expense and in addition to its defence obligations, procure continued use, modify or replace the affected item without materially reducing functionality, or, if neither is commercially reasonable, terminate the item and refund prepaid and implementation Fees on a straight-line three-year basis. Vendor may not terminate unaffected Services.

# MSA Review — Redwood Commerce Group (Customer) / Silverline Systems Ltd. (Vendor)

**Overall:** The body of this MSA is unusually customer-favorable (IP assignment, perpetual embedded-tech licence, 45-day terms, mutual cap with broad Excluded Claims, data return, transition assistance). However, **six clauses are materially off-market against Customer and contradict the rest of the document** — they read as inserted terms and should be struck or rewritten. There are also several **structural gaps** (no SLA, no security assurance rights, empty Section 23, duplicate numbering) and a **conflict-of-terms hierarchy that subordinates the negotiated MSA to vendor exhibits**.

Positions below are market-standard customer positions; I have not applied a company playbook.

---

## A. Priority 1 — Strike or rewrite (material, one-sided, internally inconsistent)

**1. Exclusivity — p0013 (first "2.2")**
"Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term." This locks Customer out of all other analytics providers for three years with no volume commitment, pricing protection, or performance condition, and it **directly contradicts p0012 (2.1) and p0050 (12.3)**.
→ **Delete in full.** If Vendor insists, cap at a named product line, condition on continuous SLA compliance and competitive pricing, and add a Customer right to terminate exclusivity on notice.

**2. Most-favoured-supplier obligation — p0027 (first "7.2")**
"Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier." This is an MFN *against* Customer, unbounded, unauditable, and inconsistent with p0050 (12.3), which recites that no MFC commitment exists. It also implicitly requires disclosure of other suppliers' confidential terms.
→ **Delete in full.** No substitute.

**3. Liquidated damages against Customer — p0032 (7.6)**
USD 25,000/day for "any delay in providing a dependency." No definition of "dependency" (note Section 12 is missing 12.1–12.2, so Customer responsibilities are undefined), no materiality threshold, no notice/cure, no cap, and no showing of actual loss — likely an unenforceable penalty under NY law, but litigation-inviting and one-sided (Vendor bears no reciprocal LDs for missed dates).
→ **Delete.** Replace with the standard excusable-delay construct:

> *"If Customer fails to perform a dependency expressly identified in the applicable Order Form or implementation plan, and that failure actually and materially delays Vendor's performance, Vendor's affected dates will be extended day-for-day and Vendor may recover documented, reasonable idle-resource costs actually incurred, provided Vendor gave Customer written notice of the dependency failure and a reasonable opportunity (not less than ten business days) to cure. This is Vendor's sole remedy for Customer delay."*

**4. Auto-renewal with 180-day notice — p0035 (8.2)**
Evergreen 12-month renewals requiring notice six months before each anniversary; a missed diary entry commits Customer to a further year at CPI/3% uplift (p0036).
→ **Reduce non-renewal notice to 30–60 days** and, preferably, make renewal at Customer's election:

> *"Each Order Form expires at the end of its stated term unless Customer elects renewal in writing. If an Order Form provides for automatic renewal, either Party may prevent renewal by written notice at least thirty (30) days before the end of the then-current term."*

**5. Non-solicit / no-hire — p0051 (12.4)**
"Any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term," for 18 months, covering *engagement* as well as solicitation. This is effectively a no-hire covering Vendor's entire workforce (including people Customer never met), is unilateral, and contradicts p0050 (12.3), which expressly preserves Customer's right to hire responders to general recruitment.
→ **Rewrite as mutual and narrow:**

> *"During the term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, neither Party will knowingly solicit for employment any employee of the other who was directly and substantially engaged in performing or receiving the Services. This does not restrict general advertising, recruiter searches not targeted at the other Party, or hiring any person who responds to such efforts or who approaches a Party unsolicited."*

**6. Vendor audit of Customer — p0093 (22.1)**
"Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records." Unlimited, unannounced, and remote-access rights are unacceptable (privileged material, other suppliers' data, Customer's own security posture) and **contradict p0094 (22.2)**, which bars direct system access.
→ **Replace 22.1 with:**

> *"No more than once per twelve months, on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, Vendor may verify Customer's usage of the Services. Verification will be conducted first by Customer self-certification based on Vendor's own usage telemetry; only if that is reasonably inconclusive may Vendor engage an independent auditor (not a Customer competitor) bound by confidentiality, during business hours, in a manner that does not disrupt Customer's operations. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems, networks, or facilities directly. Vendor bears its own and the auditor's costs, subject to Section 22.2."*

---

## B. Priority 2 — Missing protections (gaps, not bad clauses)

**7. No service levels or service credits.** Section 3 contains only 3.1. Yet p0007 (1.5) references "service credits," p0014 (2.2) references a "service-level exhibit," and p0040 (9.3) gives termination for repeatedly missing a "critical service level" — none of which exist in this document. As drafted, Customer has **no remedy for downtime** short of material-breach termination.
→ Attach an SLA exhibit before signature: uptime commitment (e.g., 99.9% excluding properly noticed maintenance), support response/resolution targets, automatic credits without a claim requirement, chronic-failure termination right with refund, and an express statement that **credits are not Customer's sole or exclusive remedy** and do not limit Section 21.

**8. No security assurance or audit rights for Customer; Section 23 is an empty heading (p0096).** Section 17 states substantive controls but gives Customer no way to verify them, and no incident obligations beyond notice.
→ Populate Section 23:

> *"Vendor shall, annually and on request: (a) provide its current SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent) report and remediation plan for any exceptions; (b) provide an executive summary of its most recent independent penetration test and confirmation of remediation of high/critical findings; (c) complete Customer's reasonable security questionnaire; and (d) on a Security Incident or material control failure, permit Customer or its independent assessor to audit Vendor's controls relevant to Customer Data. Vendor shall retain records sufficient to verify Fees, usage, and compliance for three years and make them available on reasonable notice."*

Also add to 17.2: Vendor must investigate, contain, and remediate at its cost; preserve forensic evidence; cooperate with Customer's investigation; **not notify regulators, data subjects, or the public in a manner identifying Customer without Customer's prior written consent** (except as legally required); and bear reasonable notification, credit-monitoring, and call-centre costs where the incident arises from Vendor's failure.

**9. No subcontractor / subprocessor controls.** p0017 (3.1) makes Vendor responsible for subcontractors, but there is no approval, notice, objection, or flow-down right, and no data-location commitment.
→ Add: prior written notice of new material subcontractors/subprocessors handling Customer Data, a Customer objection right (with termination of affected Services if unresolved), mandatory flow-down of Sections 15–17, and a data-residency commitment (specify permitted regions) with no cross-border transfer without Customer consent and a valid transfer mechanism.

**10. Missing exhibits are referenced as incorporated.** p0064 (15.2) incorporates "the Parties' data-processing addendum"; p0014 and p0056 reference security and service-level exhibits. None are attached.
→ Do not sign until the DPA, security exhibit, and SLA are attached and cross-referenced by title and date. Confirm the DPA covers CCPA/CPRA service-provider language, GDPR/UK Art. 28 terms, SCCs if applicable, sub-processor terms, and deletion/return consistent with Section 11.

**11. No Customer termination for convenience.** Customer can exit only for breach, insolvency, security/SLA/legal failures (9.1–9.3) or force majeure (27.3).
→ Add: *"Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience on sixty (60) days' written notice; Vendor will refund prepaid Fees for the terminated period and Customer will pay for Services performed and non-cancellable third-party costs actually incurred through the effective date."* At minimum secure this for professional-services Order Forms.

**12. No survival clause.** There is no provision listing surviving sections (confidentiality, IP, indemnity, liability, data return, transition, governing law).
→ Add a standard survival provision to Section 30.

1. **Do not sign** until the six Priority 1 clauses are struck/rewritten — items 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 each contradict other clauses in the same document, so Vendor should have little principled basis to resist.
2. **Condition signature** on attachment of the SLA, security exhibit, and DPA (item 10) — the Agreement already assumes they exist.
